experiment: E55 Amendment 2 ($0 confirmatory test of a post-hoc rule): do the slow all-spurious fine-tunes W1 and W1s1 at 10K answer the 'third' rule on fresh natural rows?
filed: 2026-10-29, before any run of experiments/pcfg_anchors/amend2.py; no model has read the fresh rows. The rule 'third' was found after Amendment 1's run by looking at its 8,000 rows (reports/analyses/2026-10-29_analysis_e55-stage-a.md, Amendment 1; exploration scripts ~/commute-data/scratch/reuse-lead/e55-a1-writer/explore.py, cfixed.py). This filing tests it on rows never looked at. Never edited after the run (a dated report instead). Same day, still before any run: the c read was changed at the lead's request after reports/reviews/2026-10-29_review_e55-amend1-analysis.md (findings 1, 4, 6): a within-c correlation with count(a) does not separate rules (third 0.78, mid 0.82 on amend1's rows), so it is replaced by the best rule of count c alone against the rule's share; W2 at 1K added to the third-rule predictions (T4).
why: On amend1's rows W1 and W1s1 at 10K answer third on 97.8% and 98.1% of all rows and on all 92 rows where third differs from the four filed rules; W2 at 10K follows mid (Amendment 1, AM3). A rule fitted after looking needs a filed read on fresh rows before it is reported as a finding.
code: experiments/pcfg_anchors/amend2.py (imports amend1's rule_answers, counts, bar_read, eval_texts); cluster/pcfg_anchors.sbatch amend2 (debug QoS, --time 00:10:00, no training); output results/amend2.json, or results/amend2_control_miss.json and exit 1 when a control misses; per-row answers results/large/amend2/answers/<state>.npy with the rows' (a, b, c) in results/large/amend2/counts.npy; log results/large/amend2/amend2.log.

constants.rows_seed: default_rng([EVAL_SEED = 1, 72]), natural texts (pcfg.sample_texts), the same rows for every state. amend1 used [1, 70] (its rows) and [1, 71] (its formula check). Disjoint: no text of the 20,000 equals any of amend1's 8,000 (checked in code, a control; measured 0 before filing).

definitions.rows: 20,000 fresh natural window texts, each asked 'C b 40'. Answer = argmax at `=` in fp32 eval mode (interchange.run_at_art) as a count (token - NUM0); a non-number answer (count < 0) equals no rule. a, b, c = window counts, a + b + c = 40 (asserted); d = b - a - 1.

rules.mid: a + 1 + trunc(d / 2), the midpoint of a + 1 and b rounded towards a + 1 (amend1).
rules.third: the nearest integer to (2 (a + 1) + b) / 3 = a + 1 + d / 3, one third of the way from a + 1 to b. Ties: none can occur, since d / 3 has fractional part 0, 1/3 or 2/3, never 1/2. Computed in integers as a + 1 + floor((d + 1) / 3); the code asserts it equals numpy rint of the fraction on every row (control). As in explore.py (np.rint((2 (a + 1) + b) / 3)). On spurious rows (d = 0) third = a + 1 = b, the label (control).

definitions.distinct_rows: for each of the five rules: the rows where its answer differs from every other of the five. Measured on the fresh rows before filing (model-free): a_plus_1 9,547, b 11,974, mid 1,342, a 8,397, third 219 (b - a in {-8, -7, -6, -5, 5, 7}: the tails). Adding third shrinks mid's rows to b - a in {-8..-5, -3, 5, 7}.
definitions.S_r: share of r's distinct rows answered with r's answer; nan under min_rows = 100 rows.
definitions.overall_r: share of all 20,000 rows answered with r's answer (rules overlap; not summed). other = share answered with none of the five.
definitions.rule_label: amend1's bar_read, unchanged (E9): f = the share of the rows on which the target equals its most common value (a constant answer's best); hi_read = f + 0.5 (1 - f). 'follows' iff S > hi_read; 'does not follow' iff S < lo = 0.1; else 'neither'; strict; nan -> 'neither'. Measured f / hi_read on the fresh rows: a_plus_1 0.4547 / 0.7273, b 0.3018 / 0.6509, mid 0.7116 / 0.8558, a 0.4100 / 0.7050, third 0.3379 / 0.6689.
definitions.route: the one rule labelled 'follows'; none -> 'mixed'; two or more -> 'ambiguous: r1+r2'. Unlike amend1 there is no rounding read: a route 'mid' whose mid c read is 'not shown' is consistent with a fixed rounding of (41 - c) / 2, i.e. count c alone (E13).
definitions.third_pairwise: for each other rule r: bar_read of third on the rows where third != r (third vs a_plus_1 9,547 rows, f / hi 0.5799 / 0.7899; vs b 16,265, 0.5520 / 0.7760; vs mid 1,342, 0.6565 / 0.8282; vs a 12,688, 0.5649 / 0.7825). Reported; scored only in T1b. Blind to coincidence with a third rule (E12).
definitions.c_read: 'not a function of count c alone': c_best = the share of all rows that the best possible rule of count c alone matches, i.e. in each count(c) group the share of the state's most common answer there, summed over groups and divided by 20,000. This is the exact best per-c answer, fitted on the same rows the state is scored on (no split): an upper bound for any rule of c alone, so it is conservative for 'beats'. For r in {third, mid}: gap_r = overall_r - c_best; 'beats count c alone' iff gap_r > c_margin = 0.05 (strict, absolute); else 'not shown'. Noise floor: binomial sd of each share ~0.003 at 20,000 rows, so of the gap ~0.004; the in-sample fit of ~20 per-c answers adds an optimism of order (groups / rows) ~0.001; c_margin is ~10 sd above both. Values: on amend1's rows W1 10K c_best 0.765 vs third 0.978 (gap 0.213), W2 10K c_best 0.817 vs third 0.848 (0.031) and mid 0.918 (0.102); model-free on the fresh rows a pure third answerer has c_best 0.790 (gap 0.210), pure mid 0.857 (mid gap 0.143), c_floor and c_ceil answerers 1.0 (gaps < 0).

edge_cases.E1_empty_or_small_pool: a read on fewer than 100 rows -> S nan -> 'neither'. The rows are fixed: the smallest pool is third's distinct rows, 219 (on amend1's 8,000 rows it was 92, under min_rows, which is why n_rows is 20,000). Pool sizes reported beside every share.
edge_cases.E2_zero_denominator: overall shares and c_best divide by 20,000; S only when n >= 100; const_floor of an empty pool nan; every count(c) group in c_best is non-empty (built from the values present).
edge_cases.E3_ties: S == hi_read or S == lo -> 'neither'; gap == c_margin -> 'not shown' (strict). third has no .5 ties (definitions).
edge_cases.E4_uncovered: two rules following -> 'ambiguous'; none -> 'mixed'. The five distinct masks are mutually exclusive, so an exact answerer never reads ambiguous.
edge_cases.E5_NaN: S nan only by E1; c_best and the gaps are never nan (fixed denominator, non-empty groups).
edge_cases.E7_non_number: equals no rule (other); in c_best a non-number is an answer like any other. Checked: an all-non-number answerer reads route mixed, c_best 1.0, gaps -1.0, 'not shown'.
edge_cases.E9_constant_answer: constants 13 and 14 read route mixed and c_best 1.0, so 'not shown' for third and mid (checked through the code); constant 14 reads 'neither' (not 'does not follow') for third, S 0.142.
edge_cases.E10_mixtures: checked: third with 10% of rows replaced by mid reads route third (S_third 0.90); a 50/50 mixture of third and mid reads mixed (S_third 0.54, S_mid 0.50). So 'follows third' asks for third on roughly 85% or more of its own rows.
edge_cases.E12_pairwise_coincidence: a pairwise read can 'follow' through another rule: a pure a answerer reads 'follows' for third vs mid (0.837 > 0.828), and pure mid reads 'follows' for third vs a + 1, b and a. So pairwise reads are scored only together (T1b: all four), and the joint distinct read carries T1.
edge_cases.E13_c_answerer_reads_mid: a pure c_floor or c_ceil answerer reads route mid (S_mid 0.987, 1.000) because mid and the count-c roundings differ only on a few of mid's rows; its c_best is 1.0, so the mid c read is 'not shown'. So 'mid' in T2 requires the mid c read 'beats count c alone'. The c read is also passed by any answerer that matches the rule more often than its own best c-alone rule: a pure a + 1 answerer 'beats' for third (0.52 vs 0.40), so the c read only says the state is not c alone, never which rule it follows.

T0_controls.claim: The read works on answerers whose rule is known.

rows.formula: third's integer form equals rint((2 (a + 1) + b) / 3) on every fresh row; third = b on 2,000 spurious texts (seed [1, 72, 2]); no fresh text equals any of amend1's 8,000. Expected true (checked).
rows.synthetic: model-free answerers through the same read: pure a_plus_1, b, mid, a, third each read route = their own rule; constants 13 and 14 and an all-non-number answerer read route mixed; c read 'beats count c alone' for third on the pure third answerer and for mid on the pure mid answerer, and 'not shown' for both on c_floor, constant 14 and non-number. All checked before filing.
rows.N1_10K: N1 at 10K: overall_b >= 0.95 and S_b >= 0.95 (positive control; amend1 read 1.000).
rows.W0_LOW: LOW (= W0 and the do-nothing reference) asked 'C b 40': overall_a >= 0.95.

T0_controls.threshold: each model row >= control_min = 0.95, inclusive, absolute; each formula and synthetic row true
T0_controls.stop: any miss -> results/amend2_control_miss.json and exit 1 before any W state is read; amend2.json is not written.
T0_controls.lean: certain for formula and synthetic rows (checked); 97% for each model row (amend1 read 1.000 and 0.9999 on its rows).

W0_expected.note: LOW is both W0 and the do-nothing reference (a zero-step fine-tune).
W0_expected.expected: route a; overall_a ~1.0; overall_third ~0.366 (the share of rows where third = a, model-free); S_third ~0, label 'does not follow'; S for a_plus_1, b, mid ~0; other ~0; c_best ~0.40, third gap ~ -0.04 and mid gap ~ -0.09, both 'not shown' (LOW answers a, a function of a alone, which a rule of c alone cannot match either; the read is about third and mid, not about a). N1 10K: route b, gaps ~ -0.22, 'not shown'.

T1_W1_10K_third.claim: W1 10K and W1s1 10K each: third labelled 'follows' (S_third > hi_read 0.6689 on its 219 rows), route third (no other rule following), and overall_third >= all_row_min = 0.95 (inclusive, absolute).
T1_W1_10K_third.lean: 85% each: on amend1's rows overall_third 0.978 and 0.981 and third on all 92 of its distinct rows (in-sample, the rows the rule was found on). Against: the distinct rows are the tails (|b - a| >= 5), seen only 92 times; a rule fitted after looking can overfit there.
T1_W1_10K_third.blind_to: the mechanism (a rule match is behaviour); rules outside the five.
T1_W1_10K_third.noise_floor: binomial sd: 0.001 for overall at 0.98 on 20,000 rows; 0.009 for S_third at 0.98 on 219 rows; seed-to-seed (W1 vs W1s1, amend1 rows) 0.003 overall.

T1b_W1_10K_pairwise.claim: W1 10K and W1s1 10K: third labelled 'follows' on each of its four pairwise pools (third vs a_plus_1, b, mid, a).
T1b_W1_10K_pairwise.blind_to: E12: alone each pairwise read can pass through another rule; scored only as all four.

T1c_W1_10K_not_c_alone.claim: W1 10K and W1s1 10K: third c read 'beats count c alone' (overall_third - c_best > 0.05).
T1c_W1_10K_not_c_alone.lean: 95% (in-sample c_best 0.765 and 0.768 vs third 0.978 and 0.981, gaps 0.213; a pure third answerer has gap 0.210 on the fresh rows).
T1c_W1_10K_not_c_alone.blind_to: which two counts: since a + b + c = 40, third = (2 (a + 1) + b) / 3 = (a + 42 - c) / 3 = (82 - b - 2c) / 3, so behaviour cannot show that the answer depends on count a specifically; it shows only that it is a function of two of the three counts, not of count c alone.

T2_W2_10K_not_third.claim: W2 10K: third labelled 'does not follow' (S_third < 0.1), overall_third < 0.95, route mid, and the mid c read 'beats count c alone' (overall_mid - c_best > 0.05; E13).
T2_W2_10K_not_third.lean: 80% (in-sample: S_mid 1.000 on 564 rows, third vs mid 0.000, overall_third 0.848; mid gap 0.102, the closest of the filed gaps to c_margin; third's distinct rows are all rows where third != mid).

T3_W1_1K_not_third.claim: W1 1K and W1s1 1K: third not labelled 'follows' and route a_plus_1.
T3_W1_1K_not_third.lean: 90% for 'not follows' (they answer a + 1, which differs from third on all of third's rows); 75% for route a_plus_1 (in-sample S 0.82 and 0.86 against hi 0.73). Reported beside: whether S_third < 0.1.

context_not_scored.trajectory: amend1's re-runs of W1 and W1s1 (results/large/amend1/, steps 1K, 2K, 3K, 5K, 7K, 10K): one run per seed sampled six times, sibling runs of a2's (max |dw| 0.0024), not anchors. Reported: overall_third and S_third per step; expected to rise from 1K to 10K, no threshold on the shape.

T4_W2_1K_third.claim: W2 1K: third labelled 'follows' (S_third > 0.6689) and route third; overall_third < 0.95.
T4_W2_1K_third.lean: 60% for follows and route third (in-sample overall_third 0.899, third on 90 of its 92 distinct rows, every pairwise read 'follows'; but the state is mid-way between rules at 1K and the tails may differ); 85% for overall_third < 0.95 (0.899 in-sample, sd 0.002). Reported beside: its third c read (in-sample gap 0.206).
T4_W2_1K_third.blind_to: as T1; a state that follows third on the tails but not elsewhere reads 'follows' with overall < 0.95, which is what this claim expects: third's distinct rows, not all rows.

blind_to: Behaviour only: a rule match says what the state answers, not how. Since a + b + c = 40 on every row, any rule of two counts is a rule of any other two: third = (2 (a + 1) + b) / 3 = (a + 42 - c) / 3 = (82 - b - 2c) / 3. So behaviour cannot separate b from c, and cannot show that the answer depends on count a specifically; it shows a function of two of the three counts, and the c read only rules out count c alone. Rules outside the five fall into other.
positive_control: T0: N1 10K on rule b and LOW on rule a (model); pure third, mid, a + 1, b, a, constant and non-number answerers through the same read, each reading its own route; c read on pure third and pure mid ('beats') and on c_floor, a constant and non-numbers ('not shown').
not_run: The scoring code was checked model-free through cpu-run on the 20,000 fresh rows (pools, floors, all synthetic answerers, mixtures, non-number) and on amend1's saved answers (in-sample, quoted in the leans as such); no model has read the fresh rows.
